marks.gloss_en: ...except the day of the king's army, when he prayed alone, והואי יחיד שלא בחבר עיר -- the one time he prayed alone, he was an individual not in a chever ir
except the day the king's army came to the city and the Rabbis were troubled and did not pray, and I prayed as an individual, and I was an individual not in a chever ir
אני ראיתי את רבי ינאי דצלי והדר צלי -- R' Yochanan saw R' Yannai pray and pray again (Steinsaltz: the second prayer was musaf, so R' Yannai acted against R' Yehuda's view; the text does not say so)
ודילמא מעיקרא לא כוון דעתיה ולבסוף כוון דעתיה -- perhaps at first he did not direct his mind and at the end he did, so the second prayer was a repetition, not musaf
R' Yochanan: I saw R' Yannai pray and then pray again
R' Yannai: the halakha is not as R' Yehuda, who said it in R' Elazar ben Azarya's name
מאן דאמר כדי שתתחונן -- דכתיב ואתחנן אל ה'
ומאן דאמר כדי שתתחולל -- דכתיב ויחל משה
the one who said 'pleading': for it is written 'and I pleaded with the Lord' (Deut 3:23)
לפי שאין בית דין מקדשין את החדש אלא ביום -- Rav's own stated reason
one who erred and did not mention the New Moon at arvit is not made to repeat
מכדי רב טעמא קאמר, מה לי חסר ומה לי מלא?! -- Rav gave a reason (the court sanctifies only by day), and it holds in a full and a deficient month alike
Rav Ashi: rather, there is no difference [between a full and a deficient month] -- so in a deficient month too he is not made to repeat
how long should one wait between one prayer and the next?
Ameimar: Rav's statement is reasonable in a full month
one may stand to pray only from gravity of mind
והאמר רבי אליעזר: לעולם ימוד אדם את עצמו... ואם לאו אל יתפלל -- one who cannot concentrate should not pray at all, so he would not have prayed the first time (= p_r_eliezer_yamod_atzmo)
Rav: the halakha is as R' Yehuda, who said it in R' Elazar ben Azarya's name
והתניא: טעה ולא הזכיר של ראש חדש... אין מחזירין אותו -- omitting the New Moon does not require repeating the prayer (= p_baraita_ein_machazirin_rch)
one who erred and did not mention the New Moon is not made to repeat: in arvit, for he can say it in shacharit; in shacharit, for he can say it in musaf; in musaf, for he can say it in mincha
R' Ami, though there were thirteen synagogues in Tiberias, prayed only between the pillars where he studied
R' Yochanan: they taught it [the baraita] of [one praying in] the congregation
ממאי? דילמא חנה שאני, דהוות מרירא לבא טובא -- perhaps Hannah is different, for her heart was very embittered
ממאי? דילמא דוד שאני, דהוה מצער נפשיה ברחמי טובא -- perhaps David is different, for he afflicted himself greatly in prayer
R' Yehoshua ben Levi: the source is 'bow to the Lord in the beauty [behadrat] of holiness' (Ps 29:2) -- do not read behadrat but becherdat, 'in the trembling'
ממאי? דילמא לעולם אימא לך הדרת ממש, כי הא דרב יהודה הוה מציין נפשיה והדר מצלי -- perhaps read 'beauty' literally, as Rav Yehuda adorned himself and then prayed
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: the source is 'serve the Lord in fear and rejoice with trembling' (Ps 2:11)
וגילו ברעדה כתיב! -- it is written 'rejoice with trembling'
Abaye, sitting before Rabba, was very joyful
אנא תפילין מנחנא -- I am wearing tefillin
בכל עצב יהיה מותר כתיב? -- it is written 'in all sorrow there is profit'
R' Yirmeya, sitting before R' Zeira, was very joyful
אנא תפילין מנחנא -- I am wearing tefillin
R' Elazar: the source is 'and she was bitter of soul' (I Sam 1:10, Hannah's prayer)
R' Yosei b'R' Chanina: the source is 'but I, by Your abundant kindness, will enter Your house; I will bow toward Your holy sanctuary in fear of You' (Ps 5:8)
'rejoice with trembling' means: where there is rejoicing, there should be trembling
